name: Snowflake
tagline: Fully managed cloud data warehouse with separate storage and compute, now spanning AI and apps.
description: Snowflake is a cloud-only analytical database that stores data in its own compressed columnar format on object storage and runs queries on independently sized virtual warehouses. Its big win is operational: no indexes, vacuuming or distribution keys to tune, near-instant zero-copy clones, time travel, and secure data sharing across accounts and clouds. It has grown into a broad platform (Snowpark, Cortex AI functions, Iceberg tables, Postgres), but at its core it remains the default choice for teams that want a SQL warehouse with almost no DBA work and are willing to pay per credit for it.

pricing.notes: Compute billed per second in credits per warehouse size; storage billed per TB-month. 30-day trial with free credits.

scale.notes: Multi-cluster warehouses scale out concurrency; database replication and failover across regions and clouds.

strengths: Near-zero administration: no indexes, vacuum or distribution keys to manage
Independent virtual warehouses isolate ETL, BI and data science workloads
Zero-copy cloning and time travel make dev/test copies and recovery trivial
Secure data sharing and Marketplace across accounts, regions and clouds
Semi-structured VARIANT data queried with plain SQL
Runs on AWS, Azure and GCP with the same feature set
weaknesses: Credit-based pricing gets expensive with always-on or poorly sized warehouses
Closed storage format for native tables (Iceberg tables are the escape hatch)
Not designed for sub-second, high-concurrency user-facing analytics
useCases: Governed data platform for ML and AI features
notIdealFor: Tight fixed budgets with spiky ad-hoc usage
